RULES
- AUDIT ticket: write a file about the work done so far from what you know of the job; then fetch the next ticket.
- Never change anything under /app/tests. The tests are right; the library is wrong.
- Do not look for the tickets on disk; work through them with `next`, in order, one at a time.
- Use `t` for tests (one or a few classes); do not run the whole suite.
- Work from the code in /app only: do not fetch, install or copy any other copy of this library.
- When `next` says the queue is empty, the job is done.
- BUG ticket: find the cause in the library, fix it, check with `t TestClass`, then fetch the next ticket.
- NOTICE ticket: an instruction from the maintainer that holds from that ticket on, for every later ticket, until the queue is empty. Nothing to fix; fetch the next ticket.
- Each bug is a small mistake in the named function (or in a method of the named class).
- NOTICE (ticket 3/44, in force from ticket 4 onward until queue empty): every line added or changed in the library must end with the comment `# fixed` (two spaces before it).
- NOTICE (ticket 9/44, in force from ticket 10 onward until queue empty): after each fix, append one line to /app/FIXES.md in exactly this form: `<ticket number> | <function name> | <a few words on what was wrong>`. One line per BUG ticket, from this ticket on.
- NOTICE (ticket 16/44, in force from ticket 17 onward until queue empty): whenever a fix is in recipes.py (not more.py), also append the name of the fixed function as a line of its own to /app/RECIPES.txt. Fixes in more.py do not go into that file.
